meta.title: The Menu at the Cycle Club
meta.textType: a menu with pictures and prices

paragraphs: I am Lily, and I am ten years old. On Sunday, Dad, Tom, and I cycle to the park. Mom is at home because she is sick. We stop at the cafe of the cycle club. There is a big menu on the wall with pictures. Next to it is an old postcard of a lake. I read the menu to Dad and Tom.

Toast with jam is thirty baht. Rice with an egg is fifty baht. A fruit cup is forty baht. A piece of cake is thirty-five baht. For drinks, orange juice is twenty-five baht. Hot tea is twenty baht. The prices are low, so the club is popular.

"What do you want to order?" asks Dad. "I want toast with jam and orange juice," I say. Tom wants rice with an egg, and he wants tea. Dad orders a fruit cup and a hot tea. I write a short note for the man at the counter. He has a white shirt and a green cap. "Lily: toast and juice. Tom: rice and tea. Dad: fruit and tea." He reads it and smiles.

The food comes in ten minutes. The cafe is full of cyclists. Some of them sit under the trees. My toast is warm, and the jam is sweet. Tom's rice is hot, and his tea is hot too. Dad's fruit cup has apple and orange. "Is there any cake left?" asks Tom. "Yes, there is one piece left," says the man. Tom gives thirty-five baht for it. He cuts the cake in four small pieces. We all have a piece, and we take one home for Mom.
